newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca leads sector up after U.S. buying.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca leads sector up after U.S. buying.

text.p: Shares in Zeneca Group led shares in other UK drug companies higher after strong U.S. buying overnight, traders and analysts said.
At 0833 GMT, shares in Zeneca were up 26-1/2p to 1573-1/2p.
Zeneca's ADRs were bolstered on news that the U.S. Federal Drug Administration cleared Accolate tablets for the preventative and chronic treatment of asthma, traders said.
Shares in Zeneca tumbled yesterday in London, after German chemicals and drug group Bayer AG ruled out a takeover, saying the British pharmaceutical concern is too expensive.

Shares in Glaxo Wellcome climbed 17-1/2p to to 993-1/2p, after stretching to a record peak 994p. The shares garnered additional support from news that the UK drug giant won a recommendation for approval for a lower dose, over the counter version of its ulcer drug Zantac in six European countries.
"The main thing was the U.S. buying, but all of this other good news adds to the momentum in the sector," said an analyst.
Expectations that brokerage Credit Lyonnais Laing is preparing to upgrade Glaxo soon also contributed to the rally, traders said.
Elsewhere in the sector, SmithKline Beecham registered a 13p gain to 767-1/2p.
